reader_evidence.answer: No reshuffle or declining: each missing draw deals each surviving fighter 2 damage, twice.

operative_units.text: - Drawing cards, whether from maneuver or an effect, is **mandatory unless explicitly optional**.

summary_support.text:

source_passages.text: **Can the six Voyages without a BOOST value pay for BOOST?** No. They have **no BOOST value**, rather than a printed zero, and cannot be discarded as BOOST payment. **Voyage Home is the exception: it has BOOST 1.** The original components identify these cards. Designer/publisher Justin Jacobson’s [October 17, 2019 explanation](https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/2294803/any-rule-of-thumb-for-boost-values) confirms that the omissions intentionally prevent Sinbad from dumping Voyages into his discard pile this way. This original-fighter clarification does not introduce other sets’ rules.

**BOOST movement:** during a maneuver, discard **1 card from your hand** to add its printed **BOOST value** (the small circled number, not its combat value) to the movement value for this maneuver. Each of your fighters receives that allowance. For **any permitted BOOST**, add the discarded card’s BOOST value and **ignore that card’s effects**, whether the BOOST modifies movement or an attack. A card that cannot be played because its fighter is defeated **can still be discarded to BOOST**. Effects may separately permit boosting attacks; boosting is not otherwise a universal option.

facts.reason: Both expressly prohibit BOOST payment with the six Voyages lacking a BOOST value, so this cannot be used to deposit them into discard.

source_passages.text: **Historical reference, superseded August 2025:** the original interpretation removed the ability BOOST even from Excalibur against Feint. Designer Justin Jacobson [confirmed that prior intent on January 2, 2021](https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/2455319/article/36640902#36640902). Under that historical interpretation only, Excalibur retained value 6 after cancellation. The publisher’s 2025 erratum replaces this historical ruling for current play.

**King Arthur:** Arthur and Merlin each use **move 2** during maneuver, before any BOOST. When **Arthur attacks**, he may BOOST the attack by playing a hand card **face down alongside his attack card**. Add that card’s BOOST value, ignoring its effects; the BOOST card is discarded. If the opponent **cancels the effects on Arthur’s attack card**, this ability’s BOOST is **discarded without effect**. **Excalibur exception (official 2025 erratum):** Excalibur has no printed effects to cancel, so Feint does not remove the ability BOOST from a textless Excalibur attack. The BOOST still increases its attack value; the ordinary final discard of played cards still applies. See the sourced FAQ below. This is Arthur’s ability, not Merlin’s. **Noble Sacrifice** separately permits another BOOST during combat, in addition to the ability’s BOOST, if its effect is not canceled.

1. Resolve **IMMEDIATELY** card effects.
2. Resolve **DURING COMBAT** card effects.
3. Determine combat result: defender takes attack value minus defense value, to a minimum of zero. If no defense card, take the attack value. Reduce the defending fighter’s health by the damage dealt. Defense does not itself deal return damage.
4. Resolve **AFTER COMBAT card effects**. A defeated fighter’s played card still resolves its after-combat effects **unless the game has already ended**.
5. Resolve other after-combat game effects, such as a hero’s special ability.
6. Finally place all played cards in their respective **face-up discard piles**.

facts.reason: The answer is expressly historical and removes the ability BOOST even for textless Excalibur, consistent with the historical quotation.

reader_evidence.answer: The six non-Home Voyages have no BOOST value and cannot pay for BOOST. Voyage Home has BOOST 1 and may pay. An absent BOOST value is not a printed zero.

summary_support.required_fact: No; six non-Home Voyages have no BOOST value and cannot be used as BOOST payment

source_passages.text: **Can the six Voyages without a BOOST value pay for BOOST?** No. They have **no BOOST value**, rather than a printed zero, and cannot be discarded as BOOST payment. **Voyage Home is the exception: it has BOOST 1.** The original components identify these cards. Designer/publisher Justin Jacobson’s [October 17, 2019 explanation](https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/2294803/any-rule-of-thumb-for-boost-values) confirms that the omissions intentionally prevent Sinbad from dumping Voyages into his discard pile this way. This original-fighter clarification does not introduce other sets’ rules.

**BOOST movement:** during a maneuver, discard **1 card from your hand** to add its printed **BOOST value** (the small circled number, not its combat value) to the movement value for this maneuver. Each of your fighters receives that allowance. For **any permitted BOOST**, add the discarded card’s BOOST value and **ignore that card’s effects**, whether the BOOST modifies movement or an attack. A card that cannot be played because its fighter is defeated **can still be discarded to BOOST**. Effects may separately permit boosting attacks; boosting is not otherwise a universal option.

facts.reason: Both expressly prohibit BOOST payment with the six Voyages lacking a BOOST value, so this cannot be used to deposit them into discard.

source_passages.text: **Historical reference, superseded August 2025:** the original interpretation removed the ability BOOST even from Excalibur against Feint. Designer Justin Jacobson [confirmed that prior intent on January 2, 2021](https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/2455319/article/36640902#36640902). Under that historical interpretation only, Excalibur retained value 6 after cancellation. The publisher’s 2025 erratum replaces this historical ruling for current play.

**King Arthur:** Arthur and Merlin each use **move 2** during maneuver, before any BOOST. When **Arthur attacks**, he may BOOST the attack by playing a hand card **face down alongside his attack card**. Add that card’s BOOST value, ignoring its effects; the BOOST card is discarded. If the opponent **cancels the effects on Arthur’s attack card**, this ability’s BOOST is **discarded without effect**. **Excalibur exception (official 2025 erratum):** Excalibur has no printed effects to cancel, so Feint does not remove the ability BOOST from a textless Excalibur attack. The BOOST still increases its attack value; the ordinary final discard of played cards still applies. See the sourced FAQ below. This is Arthur’s ability, not Merlin’s. **Noble Sacrifice** separately permits another BOOST during combat, in addition to the ability’s BOOST, if its effect is not canceled.

1. Resolve **IMMEDIATELY** card effects.
2. Resolve **DURING COMBAT** card effects.
3. Determine combat result: defender takes attack value minus defense value, to a minimum of zero. If no defense card, take the attack value. Reduce the defending fighter’s health by the damage dealt. Defense does not itself deal return damage.
4. Resolve **AFTER COMBAT card effects**. A defeated fighter’s played card still resolves its after-combat effects **unless the game has already ended**.
5. Resolve other after-combat game effects, such as a hero’s special ability.
6. Finally place all played cards in their respective **face-up discard piles**.
